subject: Re: Redwood evals - dataset format & scoring criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@finservco.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finservco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-03-18T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + next steps from today’s evals discovery call

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and really helpful context on the extraction + summarization use cases you outlined. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a customer-specific eval running on Redwood: 

What we heard:
- Primary goal: reliable extraction of transaction metadata and short summaries from semi-structured support emails and receipts.
- Constraints: latency target ~350ms p95, high precision on entity extraction (fraud flags), and strict data handling rules (PII must be scrubbed or processed in your VPC).

Recommended models to test (start small and iterate):
- Redwood-Relay-7B (q4_0) — low-cost baseline for throughput testing
- Redwood-Relay-13B (8-bit) — quality/precision baseline for extraction and summarization
- Mistral-7B-instruct — alternate architecture reference for hallucination behavior

What we need from you to run the evals on Redwood:
1) A sample dataset (CSV or JSONL, see attached prompt_set template) with ~500-1,000 labeled examples for the first pass. Columns: id, prompt, reference, metadata.
2) Scoring rules and thresholds — we’ll use the scoring template (attached) but please confirm which fields are critical (e.g., transaction_id exact match, date tolerance ± 2 days, entity-level F1 >= 0.9).
3) Security preference — hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC. If you require data to stay in your VPC, we can run the eval on Redwood Private; otherwise we’ll use a Dedicated eval pool with strict retention controls.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Redwood will run an initial eval suite (3 model variants) and provide an executive summary + per-prompt failure analysis within 10 business days after we receive the labeled sample.
- We’ll surface any quality regressions vs. your baseline and provide recommended prompt/retrieval changes.

Next steps:
- Can you share a 200-300 example sample by end of day Friday? I attached a prompt_set CSV template and an eval scoring workbook.
- I’ll have Rishi and Dev pick the exact eval configs once we have the sample.

Attachments: finserv_prompt_set_v1.csv (template), eval_scoring_template.xlsx, redwood_eval_instructions.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick sync if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — this looks good. A couple of clarification/Qs before we prepare the sample: 

1) Dataset format — for the CSV template, can you confirm exact column names and whether nested JSON in a metadata column is OK (we often include customer_id + ingestion_source as a JSON blob).
2) Scoring — the team wants to confirm thresholds. For transaction_id we need exact match; for date we can allow ± 1 day; for merchant_name we can accept F1 >= 0.88. Is semantic-similarity scoring supported (e.g., for open-ended summaries)?
3) PII handling — we will anonymize where possible, but can Redwood run the evals in our VPC? We need assurance of no intermediate retention and audit logs.

I can pull a 250-example sample by Friday if that works — we’ll anonymize and drop PII but may keep a mapping internally for verification.

One more ask: could you point me to an example eval report or benchmark output format so our stakeholders know what to expect?

Thanks,
Lisa
Director, Data Products | FinServCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@finservco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today’s evals discovery call

Hi Lisa —

Great questions — answers inline: 

1) Dataset format: both CSV and JSONL are supported. For CSV we recommend these column names: id, prompt, reference, metadata. The metadata column can be a JSON string; please escape quotes per CSV rules. For JSONL, each line should be a flat JSON object with the same keys. Example CSV row (comma-delimited):

"12345","Extract entities: <email body here>","{\"transaction_id\":\"TX123\",\"amount\":\"42.50\"}","{\"customer_id\":\"C-501\",\"source\":\"email_ingest\"}"

2) Scoring: we support exact match, token-level F1, ROUGE/ROUGE-L for summaries, and semantic-similarity using our embedding-based scorer. For semantic scoring we use cosine similarity over instruction-tuned embeddings; we can surface both raw similarity and calibrated pass/fail with a threshold. Recommended initial thresholds: transaction_id exact, date ± 1 day, entity-level F1 >= 0.88, summary semantic similarity >= 0.75. We will include per-field confusion matrices in the report.

3) PII / hosting: yes — we can run evals in your Private VPC (no data egress to hosted control plane) or in a Dedicated eval pool with data redaction and 7-day retention. For Private runs we provide KMS integration and audit logs. I’ve attached the redwood_eval_instructions.pdf which covers upload mechanics and retention controls.

Example report: https://redwood.inference/internal/benchmarks/eval-run-logs (I’ll share a sanitized sample PDF after the first run).

Rishi / Dev — can you confirm the default eval config you’ll use (batch size, max tokens, seed) so I can pass that to FinServ?

Lisa — if you can share the 250-example anonymized CSV (or JSONL) by EOD Friday that’s perfect. If you need more time, Tuesday next week is fine too.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today’s evals discovery call

Quick technical notes from the infra side: 

- Default eval config we’ll start with: batch_size=32, max_tokens=1024, temperature=0.0, deterministic seed for reproducibility. We’ll run each model variant across the full sample and preserve raw outputs + token logits for deeper analysis.
- Supported input formats: CSV (columns: id,prompt,reference,metadata-json) or JSONL (flat objects). We’ll ingest the metadata JSON as a string and parse into structured fields for grouping.
- Scoring pipeline: we compute exact match and token-F1 using the reference, ROUGE-L for summaries, and an embedding-based semantic similarity (sentence-transformers style) for open-ended outputs. We also run an entailment model as a secondary check when possible.
- Quality regression detection: we’ll compare the new run to your baseline (if you can provide previous outputs) and flag regressions where delta(metric) < -0.05 (5 percentage points) on any critical metric. We’ll surface per-prompt failures and cluster them by failure mode (e.g., format errors, hallucinations, partial extraction).
- Infra note: For large datasets (>5k rows) we recommend using a Dedicated eval pool to avoid contention. For your 250-1k sample the Dedicated eval pool is fine and significantly cheaper than a private deployment.

Action items for FinServCo:
- Share anonymized sample (CSV/JSONL) and indicate which fields are critical for pass/fail rules.
- If you have an existing baseline, share it with a mapping to id values.

I’ll open a run once the sample is uploaded to the Drive link Marissa shared.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior ML Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
